title: What a decision costs

blocks.text: A rail operator's planners ask, for every track renewal, "what would it cost to decide the other way?". `costs.py` already builds the one-budget selection: a binary per renewal, the budget row, a row per must-do, and the most value as the objective. Write `decision_costs(projects, budget)`:

items: Solve once, to proven optimality (the module gives `EXACT`), and note which renewals are funded.
For each renewal in turn, reverse its decision: a funded one is forced out, an unfunded one forced in. Re-solve, and record the best value lost, the base optimum minus the forced optimum.

When the rules refuse the reversal, record `None`, not a number. A refused reversal is a forced model that has no plan: HiGHS ends it with `TerminationReason.INFEASIBLE` (a must-do forced out, for one). Record a number only when the re-solve ends `OPTIMAL`.

blocks.text: Build the model once and change only the reversed renewal's bounds for each re-solve, so that each reversal is priced on its own. The tests compare with brute force. About fifteen lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
from costs import Project, decision_costs

# A bus company's depot works.
works = [
    Project("Roof", 45, 25),
    Project("Wash", 35, 20),
    Project("Pits", 30, 25),
    Project("Fence", 8, 10, must_do=True),
]

for budget in (55, 70, 10):
    costs = decision_costs(works, budget)
    print(f"budget {budget}:", {pid: None if c is None else round(c, 2) for pid, c in costs.items()})

cases.says: a funded project's cost is the value the best plan loses when it is forced out
an unfunded project's cost is the value the best plan loses when it is forced in
each reversal is priced alone, with every other decision free again
a must-do forced out gets no number
